name: Mayor Lina
title: Mayor of Oakhaven

lines: Ah, a new face! Welcome to Oakhaven, traveler. I'm Lina — mayor, baker, and part-time settler of fence disputes.
Every great farmer, smith and adventurer in TerraGo started right where you're standing: tired, a little lost, and nearly broke.
Here — your Oakhaven Charter, so the guards know you belong. And two of my honey buns. The road takes it out of you.
Whispering Fields lies through the south gate. Farmland near town, and wilder things further south.

greetings: The fountain was built by the first settlers. They say a coin tossed in brings rain to Whispering Fields.
Personally, I think it brings coins to whoever cleans the fountain.
Don't let the quiet fool you. Oakhaven is growing — every season brings new faces and new trouble.
Short on Energy? Eat something! Nobody tills a field on an empty stomach.
Talk to Rowan about farming, Toren about tools, and Mira about anything with a price tag.

name: Farmer Rowan
title: Farm Supplier

lines: Name's Rowan. I sell seeds and I know dirt — the good kind.
That hoe of yours has seen better decades. Still, a worn tool in patient hands beats a fine one in lazy hands.
Carrots are the honest crop. Cheap seeds, modest price. You won't get rich off them, but they'll teach you the rhythm. Your homestead is waiting at the west end of the Whispering Fields lane.

greetings: Your homestead's at the west end of the Whispering Fields lane. Till it, plant it, water it — and come back for more seeds.
Water in the morning, harvest when it's ready, and never trust a cloud that promises rain.
Quality is what separates a farmer from someone who owns a hoe. Gold-quality carrots? Now that's a conversation.
Soil stays wet for about an hour after watering. Dry soil means a crop that sits and sulks.

name: Blacksmith Toren
title: Blacksmith

lines: Hmph. Another fresh arrival with soft hands.
I'm Toren. I forge tools, blades and armor — and I repair what you break, for a fee.
Bring me ore from the Desolate Crags, north of town, and I'll show you what real iron looks like.

greetings: Everything breaks eventually. That's what keeps me in business.
Gems from the Crags and the Glacial Depths make the finest upgrades. Bring me some.
A +10 blade is a fine thing. A +10 blade that cost you nothing is a lie.

name: Merchant Mira
title: Market Trader

lines: Well, well! A customer — or a competitor? In Oakhaven those are often the same person.
I'm Mira. I buy low, sell high, and remember every face that haggles.
Soon these stalls open to everyone. List your goods, set your price, and let the market decide what you're worth.

greetings: The shops pay pennies. Real profit comes from other players — remember that.
Rare fish, fine ingots, gold-quality crops... scarcity is where fortunes are made.
A word of advice? Never sell the first thing you find. Learn what it's worth first.

name: Fisher Olan
title: Fisherman

lines: Shh... you'll scare the perch.
Olan. I fish. Mostly I wait, which is the bigger part of fishing.
Anyone who tells you fishing is just clicking a button has never fought a pond pike.

greetings: The big ones bite at dawn and dusk. The really big ones bite whenever they please.
Rain makes the fish hungry. Storms make them bold.
This pond looks small, but rare things live at the bottom. Rare things, and good crafting materials.

name: Miner Bram
title: Miner

lines: Bram's the name, mining's the game! The Crags are north of town: bring a good pickaxe.
Copper on the upper floors, iron deeper down, and below that... things that glitter and things that bite.
Bring a good pickaxe and plenty of food. The mine eats Energy like I eat breakfast.

greetings: The Crags are north of town. Bring a good pickaxe.
Ore in the Crags, gems deeper still, in the ice.

name: Guildmaster Kael
title: Guildmaster

lines: Welcome to the Guild Hall. I am Kael, keeper of the guild registry.
Alone, a player can farm, mine and fight. Together, a guild can topple a Stoneheart Golem and hold the market.
When you've made a name for yourself — and saved enough for the charter fee — come back and found a guild of your own.

greetings: The strongest guilds aren't the ones with the best fighters. They're the ones where the farmers feed the fighters.
Pyraxis, the Infernal Titan, sleeps in the Caldera beyond Dragon's Peak. Only a raid of the realm's best could wake him and live.
Trust is the rarest currency in TerraGo. Spend it carefully.

name: Stablemaster Hana
title: Stables

lines: Hana. I keep the horses. You look like someone who's tired of walking.
Mayor Lina told me to expect you — here's a pony from the town herd. Press Z to ride, Z again to get off.
Mounts don't like fights or tight mine tunnels. Come back when you've got gold; I've faster beasts.

greetings: Faster mounts cost more — and they're worth every coin.
A pony carries a farmer; a stag carries a legend.

name: Scout Bjorna
title: Glacial Depths

lines: Bjorna. I scout the peaks for the Guild.
Wolves on the slopes, yetis by the frozen lake — and up north, the Frost Giant himself.
He wakes every half hour or so. Bring a crowd if you mean to fight him.

greetings: Snow's deep today. Watch your step.
Seen the giant? You'd know if you had.

name: Banker Orrin
title: Oakhaven Bank

lines: Orrin, at your service. Your vault is safe with us — every coin and every carrot.
Thirty stacks to start. Bigger vaults cost a little Gold, but they never forget a thing.

greetings: Deposits, withdrawals, upgrades. What'll it be?
Safe as stone, our vaults.

name: Forgewarden Hal
title: Desolate Crags

lines: Hal. I guard the old dwarf forges on this ridge.
Magma hounds and fire spirits, and golems of black glass. Bring your best armor — and bring water.

greetings: The mountain breathes fire. Respect it.
Obsidian? The golems are made of it. Help yourself.

name: Dragon Hunter Kade
title: Dragon's Peak

lines: Kade. I hunt dragons. Mostly they hunt me.
Drakes on the slopes, dragon knights on the bridges — and at the summit, the Ancient Wyvern.
Twenty of the best fighters in TerraGo, maybe. That's what it'll take.

greetings: Fire-proof cloak? Good. Now a bigger one.
If you hear wings, run.

name: Master Aldric
title: Job Trainer

lines: You made it past Gnarlfang. Few do.
At level 40 I teach the second jobs: two roads for every class, and you may walk only one.

greetings: Strength is chosen, not given. Choose well.
At level 40 every hero must pick a path.
